items.heading: Article 2

items.text: 1. This Directive applies to children who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings. It applies until the final determination of the question whether the suspect or accused person has committed a criminal offence, including, where applicable, sentencing and the resolution of any appeal.

provisions.comment: The provisions of the italian legislation already seem to be in accordance with the article 3 of the Directive. The President Decree no 448/1988, in addition, orders that when the person’s age is uncertain (it does not know if she/he has reached the majority age or the age requested for the chargeability) the judge shall ask the opinion of an expert. If even the report does not resolve the doubts, that person shall be presumed to be a child.
provisions.textEn:
1. When the child's age is uncertain, the judge shall have an expert opinion, even on his own motion.

2. Where, even after the expert's report, there is still doubt about the child's age, it shall be presumed that the child has not reached the age of majority.

3. The provisions of paragraphs 1 and 2 shall also apply where there is reason to believe that the accused is under the age of fourteen.

provisions.textEn: Without prejudice to Article 97 of the Criminal Procedure Code, the Board of the Bar Association shall arrange lists of lawyers with a specific preparation in juvenile law.

1. The accused person is entlitled to appoint no more than two retained lawyers.
  2. The retained lawyer shall be appointed by a statement either given to the proceeding authority by the accused or her/his lawyer or forwarded by registred letter.
  3. If the person who is temporarily detained, arrest or held under precautionary detention does not appoint a retained lawyer, the latter may be appointed by his next of kin according to paragraph 2.

1. The accused person who has not appointed or no longer has a retained lawyer shall be assisted by a court-appointed lawyer.
  2. In order to ensure the effectiveness of the court-appointed defence, the Board of the Bar Association of each Court of Appeal district, through a dedicated centralised office, shall draw lists of lawyers who may be appointed by the court upon request of the judicial authority or the police. The Boards of the Bar Association shall set the criteria for the appointment of lawyers on the basis of their specific competencies, their proximity to the place of the proceedings and their availability.
  3. If the judge, the Public Prosecutor and the police must carry out an action requiring the assistance of a lawyer and the suspect or the accused does not have a lawyer, thay shall inform the lawyer, whose name is notified by the office referred to in paragraph 2, of this particular action.

provisions.comment:
While the individual assessment is explicitly required for the arrest in flagrante delicto (Art 16, c. 3 Decree 448/1988), the same is not specifically demanded for the case of temporary detention (fermo) of the child suspected of a crime. When the temporary detention is enforced by the police and not the prosecutor, this gap seems not to be filled by the general provision of Art 9 of the Decree, which only concerns the individual assessments carried out by the judge and the prosecutor. Against this backdrop, we should nevertheless take into account that the legal doctrine considers that the temporary detention can be applied in the same cases and with the same modalities foreseen for the arrest in flagrante delicto under Art 16 of the Decree. This would mean that the need to perform an individual assessment prior to the restriction of liberty should apply in this case as well, despite the lack of an explicit reference to this requirement.

Cf. Lanza, Enrico (2020): ʿIl processo penale minorileʾ , in A. Mangione and A. Pulvirenti (eds) La Giustizia Penale Minorile: Formazione, Devianza, Diritto e Processo (3rd edn, Milano, Giuffrè).

Assignment to a juvenile penal institution shall be notified to the prosecuting judicial authority. Assignment to an institution other than the one closest to the place of residence or habitual residence shall be ordered by reasoned decision and shall be subjected to authorisation by the judicial authority.

Penal institutes for adults dependent on the prison administration are distinguished in: 1) institutes for pre-trial detention; 2) institutes for the enforcement of sentences; 3) institutes for the enforcement of security measures; 4) observation centres

The project, drawn up according to the principles of personalisation of prescriptions and flexibility of execution after listening to the convicted person, takes into account her/his attitudes and personality characteristics. The project contains indications on how to cultivate relationships with the outside world and implement group life and responsible citizenship also respecting gender diversity and on the personalization of education, vocational training, as well as work, social utility, cultural, sports and leisure activities useful for social recovery and prevention of the risk of committing further crimes.

2. Upon entering the institute, psychological support is guaranteed by specialized personnel, which is also useful for the preparation of the educational project and for the prevention of the risk of acts of self-harm and suicide.

3. The project is illustrated to the condemned with comprehensible language and is constantly updated, considering the degree of adherence to the opportunities offered, the psycho-physical evolution and the path of maturation and empowerment.

items.heading: Article 13
items.subHeading: Timely and diligent treatment of cases

items.text: 1. Member States shall take all appropriate measures to ensure that criminal proceedings involving children are treated as a matter of urgency and with due diligence.

items.comment:
No specific provision exists in the Italian legal system which aims at guaranteeing a speedy trial when it comes to juvenile defendants.

Children may request the application of special proceedings, which may have also the effect of speeding up the treatment of the cause, but this is a choice that relies entirely on the defendant and does not apply to all cases of juvenile justice.

In general:

In Italy, the juvenile criminal justice system is regulated by D.P.R. 448/1988 (hereafter: the Decree): it provides for specific rules that take into account the peculiar condition of a minor. However, it is hardly a completely autonomous system: art. 1 of the Decree explicitly states that «the criminal trial of a minor is regulated by the present Decree and, for what is not provided here, by the code of criminal procedure». This general reference strongly impacts the rules of the trial in absentia.


Participation at a pre-trial stage:

The directive asks the States to ensure the right to appear in person at trial.

The Italian criminal proceeding is divided into three phases: preliminary investigation, preliminary hearing and trial.

In the Italian legislation, the right to participate in person is triggered by the decision of the prosecutor to officially bring charges: when a person is formally accused of something, she has the right to be present, even if what follows is not "trial", but still a preliminary hearing.

This difference is valid for minors and adults alike, but in the juvenile system it is particularly important.

The Italian juvenile system tries to limit the contact between the minor and the criminal proceeding as much as it can, along all international conventions and charters that call for such an arrangement. To do so, the preliminary hearing is the privileged frame for a decision: all diversion mechanisms normally take place here, and statistically it is the phase where most of the decisions occur. According to the latest data available (2017), only 3.142 cases proceeded to trial, whereas 9.189 cases were adjudicated within the preliminary hearing.

Ensuring the right to participate in person only at trial would therefore respect just the letter of the directive, but not at all the spirit.

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that children have the right to be present at their trial and shall take all necessary measures to enable them to participate effectively in the trial, including by giving them the opportunity to be heard and to express their views.

provisions.textEn:
1. If the accused, free or detained, is not present at the hearing and, even if unable to appear, has expressly waived his right to be present, the Preliminary Hearing Judge shall proceed in his absence.

2. Without prejudice to the provisions of Article 420-ter, the Preliminary Hearing Judge shall also proceed in the absence of the accused if the latter has already declared or chosen an address for service during the proceedings or has been arrested or placed under temporary detention or has been ordered a precautionary measure or has appointed a retained lawyer. The Judge shall also proceed when the accused is not present at the hearing but has been served the notice of the hearing personally or it is in any case certain that the accused is aware of the proceedings or has voluntarily avoided to be informed about either the proceedings or the documents thereof.

3. In the cases provided for in paragraph 1 and 2, the accused shall be represented by his lawyer. The accused who, after his appearance, leaves the hearing room or, after appearing at a hearing, is not present at the following hearings, shall also be considered present and represented by his lawyer.

4. The order to hold proceedings in the absence of the accused shall be revoked, also of the Preliminary Hearing Judge‟s own motion, should the accused appear in court before delivery of the decision. If the accused provides evidence to prove that his absence was due to his inculpable unawareness of the proceedings, the Judge shall adjourn the hearing and the accused may require the gathering of documents and documentary evidence according to Article 421, paragraph 3. During the first-instance trial, the accused is entitled to submit a request for evidence according to Article 493. Without prejudice to the validity of the acts duly conducted hitherto, the accused may also require the renewal of the evidence already gathered. The same procedure shall be followed if the accused proves that his absence was related to an absolute impossibility to appear due to unforeseeable circumstances, force majeure or another legal impediment, and that the proof of such impediment was produced with delay without him being liable for this.

5. The Preliminary Hearing Judge shall also revoke the order and follow the procedure referred to in Article 420-quater if it emerges that the trial should have been suspended according to the provisions of such Article because the accused was absent.

1. If the accused, also detained, does not appear at the hearing and his absence is due to an absolute impossibility to appear due to unforeseeable circumstances, force majeure or legal impediment, the Preliminary Hearing Judge, by means of an order, also of his own motion, shall adjourn the hearing and order the renewal of the notice to the accused, under Article 419, paragraph 1.

2. The Preliminary Hearing Judge shall follow the same procedure referred to in paragraph 1 when it is likely that the absence of the accused is related to an absolute impossibility to appear due to unforeseeable circumstances or force majeure. Such likelihood shall be freely evaluated by the Judge and shall not be debated later nor shall it be the basis for a further appellate remedy.

3. If the accused, also detained, does not appear at the following hearings and the conditions provided for in paragraph 1 are met, the Preliminary Hearing Judge shall adjourn the hearing, also of his own motion, and set by order the date of the new hearing, ordering the service on the accused.

4. In any case, the reading of the order setting the new hearing shall substitute the summons and the notices for those who are or must be present.

5. If the accused person's lawyer is absent, the Preliminary Hearing Judge shall decide following the provision of paragraph 1 when the absence is due to an absolute impossibility to appear due to a legal impediment, provided that this is immediately notified. Such provision shall not apply if the accused is assisted by two lawyers and the impediment involves one of these lawyers or if the lawyer who cannot attend has appointed a substitute or the accused requests to proceed without the presence of his lawyer. 

5-bis. For the effects of paragraph 5, the lawyer who promptly notified her state of pregnancy is to be considered legally impeded from attending the proceeding from the two months before the expected date of birth to three months after said date.

Suspension of trial due to absence of the accused

1. With the exception of the cases set out in Articles 420-bis and 420-ter and the cases of nullity of the service, if the accused is not present, the Preliminary Hearing Judge shall adjourn the hearing and order the notice to be served personally on the accused by the criminal police.

2. When it is impossible to serve the notice according to paragraph 1 and unless a judgment must be delivered in line with Article 129, the Preliminary Hearing Judge shall direct by order suspension of the trial against the accused who failed to appear. The provision of Article 18, paragraph 1, letter b), shall apply. The provision of Article 75, paragraph 3, shall not apply.

3. During suspension of trial, the Preliminary Hearing Judge shall, upon request of a party, gather non-deferrable evidence following the procedure established for the trial.

New searches for the accused and revocation of suspension of trial

1. At the end of the first year of the issuing of the order referred to in Article 420-quater, paragraph 2, or, even before then if deemed necessary, the Preliminary Hearing Judge shall order new searches for the accused, in order to serve the notice upon him. The Judge shall decide likewise at the end of each successive year, in case the proceedings do not resume.

2. The Preliminary Hearing Judge shall revoke the order of suspension of trial:

a) if the accused is found after the searches referred to in paragraph 1;

b) if in the meantime the accused has appointed a retained lawyer;

c) in any other case where it is certain that the accused is aware of the proceedings against him;

d) if a judgment must be delivered in line with Article 129.

3. The Preliminary Hearing Judge shall set the date for the new hearing in the order of suspension of trial,

and the notice thereof shall be served, as ordered by the Judge, upon the accused and his lawyer, the other private parties and the victim, and shall be forwarded to the Public Prosecutor.

4. During the hearing referred to in paragraph 3, the accused may submit a request according to Articles 438 and 444.

provisions.comment: This provision is not explicitly referred to in the Decree, but it is not explicitly waived or substituted either. It therefore applies to the minor pursuant to art. 1 of the Decree, as described in the general remarks.
provisions.textEn:
Spontaneous statements from the accused

1. After the introductory remarks, the President of the bench shall inform the accused of his right to provide, at any stage of the trial, the statements he considers appropriate, provided they concern the subject of the accusation and do not hinder the trial evidentiary hearing. If the accused does not keep to the subject of the accusation while making his statements, the President of the bench shall admonish him and, if the accused persists, he shall interrupt him.

2. The assistant shall transcribe integrally the statements made under paragraph 1, unless the court orders the record be drafted in summary form.

items.text: 2. Member States shall ensure that children who were not present at their trial have the right to a new trial or to another legal remedy, in accordance with, and under the conditions set out in, Directive (EU) 2016/343.

provisions.textEn:
1. The accused who has been absent for the entire duration of proceedings and has been convicted or ordered a security measure with a final judgment, can obtain the rescission of the final judgment if he can prove that his absence was due to his inculpable unawareness of the proceedings.

2. The request shall be submitted to the Court of Appeal in whose district the decision has been taken, under penalty of inadmissibility. Submission shall take place within thirty days of acknowledgement by the accused of the proceedings and shall be made either in person or through a lawyer holding a special power of attorney authenticated as per Article 583, paragraph 3.

3. The Court of Appeal shall decide in accordance with Article 127 and, should it accept the request, it shall rescind the judgment and order that the case file be forwarded to the first instance court. The provision of Article 489, paragraph 2, shall apply.

4. Articles 635 and 640 shall apply.

items.comment:
No specific provision can be found in the Law no 69/2005 - implementing the European Arrest Warrant Framework Decision - with regard to the procedural rights recognized to juvenile defendants.


The clause of Article 1(1) DPR 448/1988 combined to that of Article 39(1) Law 69/2005 should ensure that the same rights recognized to juvenile defendants in internal proceedings apply also to EAW proceedings. However, this is explicitly so only for those rights which are common to juvenile and adult defendants (Article 6 and, partially, Article 4 of this Directive).

No explicit reference is instead made with regard to the rights provided for by Article 5 and 8 of this Directive. In this regard, the transposition of Directive 2016/800 could be considered partial.

It should also be recalled, though, that at certain conditions juvenile defendants are exempted from surrender through the EAW thanks to a mandatory ground for refusal (see below, Article 18(1)(i), Law 69/2005.

  2. at the same time as communicating the payment decree, the office requires the family members of the minor to submit within one month the documentation required by Article 79 (proof of income requirements) (...);

items.comment: Article. 24 of the Constitution, concerning the right of defence for indigent persons, does not limit this right to adult defendants only. The Italian legal system provides for an income limit to have access to legal aid. In the case of minors, the family members' tax documents must be presented. However, articles 116 and 118 of Presidential Decree No 115/2002 grant an additional margin to minor defendants when a public defender is appointed. In these cases, the State advances the costs and fees to the public defender of the minor and then has the right to recover the amount paid if the judge establishes that the income limits for admission to legal aid are exceeded. In these cases, it is therefore the State itself that must take steps to verify the existence of the conditions for the repayment of the sums, since the minor or his family members do not have to submit any application for admission to legal aid (on the contrary, in the case of the adult, he must take steps to avoid the repayment of the sums by the State).

items.text: Member States shall ensure that children who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings and children who are requested persons have an effective remedy under national law in the event of a breach of their rights under this Directive.
items.heading: Article 19
items.comment:
PARTIAL IMPLEMENTATION

No specific remedy has been introduced in the Italian legal framework to address violations of the rights included in the Directive.

However, to some extent, the previously existing legislation already provided for some remedy in case of certain violations of the rights contained in this Directive. All these provisions (with the exception of Article 7 DPR 448/1988) are not specifically tailored to children, but refer to adults (and are applicable to juvenile defendants in light of the equivalence clause of Article 1 of the Presidential Decree no. 448/1988).

In this regard, it could be considered that Article 19 is indirectly but only partially implemented in Italy.


Specifically, remedies are recognized (or not recognized) as follow:


RIGHT TO INFORMATION


A) Along the same line as for adult defendants with regard to the right to be informed of the accusation, of the right to be assisted by the lawyer, of the right to legal aid, of the right to a medical examination, and of the limits of the deprivation of liberty,

and namely (see also Article 8(2) Directive 2013/12):


* in connection with the right to access to a lawyer (Articles 369, 369bis, 386(1)(a), 293(1)(a), 386(1)(a) c.p.p.): Violations of this information right are sanctioned with nullity ex Article 178 (1), let. c) c.p.p. (nullità intermedia), which may be raised also ex officio within specific time limits that follow the different phases of criminal proceedings (not after the decision of first instance for violations occurred before the trial hearing; for those occurred at trial, not after the decision of the following instance). In case of violation of Article 293 c.p.p., such nullity may also be invoked through the specific appeal remedies established against pre-trial measures (Article 309 ff c.p.p.).


* in connection with the right to be informed of the accusation ex Articles 293, 386 c.p.p.: Violations of this information rights are sanctioned with nullity ex Article 178 (1), let. c) c.p.p. (nullità intermedia), which may be raised also ex officio within specific time limits that follow the different phases of criminal proceedings (not after the decision of first instance for violations occurred before the trial hearing; for those occurred during the trial, not after the decision of the following instance). In case of violation of Article 293 c.p.p., such nullity may also be invoked through the specific appeal remedies established against pre-trial measures (Article 309 ff c.p.p.).


* in connection with the right to be informed of the accusation ex Article 415bis(2) c.p.p.: if the warnings of Article 415bis are missing, the request to proceed to trial (Article 416 c.p.p.) is sanctioned by nullity.


* in connection with the right to be informed of any changes in the information given, and specifically of potential changes in the accusation, ex Articles 423, 516, 517, 518, 520, 521, 604 c.p.p.: Violations of these information rights is sanctioned with the nullity of the decision in accordance with Article 522 c.p.p.


* in connection with the right to remain silent (Articles 63 and 64 c.p.p.): Violations of this information right are sanctioned by exclusionary rule, that is, statements obtained without the previous warning cannot be used as evidence, unless they are in favour of the suspect (cf. Cass. Sez. Un., 13 December 1996, RV 206846)


* doubious is the effectiveness of remedies in connection with the right to be informed of the accusation ex Article 335 c.p.p., for which only disciplinary sanctions might be applicable, cf. S. Ciampi, Diritto all'informazione nei procedimenti penali: il recepimento low profile della Direttiva 2012/13/UE da parte del d. lsg. 1° luglio 2014 n. 101. Letter of Rights e Full Disclosure nel procedimento penale italiano, in Dir. pen. cont., p. 9; contra P. Gualtieri, Registro delle notizie di reato: i problemi del dopo riforma. Il punto di vista di un avvocato, in Dir. pen. proc., 1996, p. 498)


B) No specific remedy exists with regard to the right of the defendants to: have the holder of parental responsibility informed, as well as to be informed of: the right to privacy, the right to be accompanied by holder of parental responsibility, the right to be present at trial, the right to an effective remedy and the right to a specific treatment. As illustrated above, these information rights have indeed not been implemented in the Italian legislation.


C) Also, no remedy exists in case the information rights are provided in a language that is substantially not comprehensible by the defendant




RIGHT TO ACCESS TO A LAWYER


Remedies concerning this profile are the same provided for adults (see Article 10, Directive 2013/48):


A) If certain investigative or trial acts are carried out without the necessary presence of the lawyer, the act is affected by "absolute nullity" (nullità assoluta, art. 178(1) (c) c.p.p.). Complaints about this invalidity may be raised at any time by parties or ex officio until the decision becomes final (res judicata, art. 648 c.p.p.).

The declaration of nullity by the judge may have three effects: i) the spreading of the nullity to the acts following the invalid act; ii) the renewal of the invalid act; iii) the regression of the proceedings at the stage in which the defective act was committed.


Such acts are:

- interview of the suspect (that participates in a state of liberty) carried out by police (art. 350(1) and 370(1) c.p.p.)

- confrontation delegated by the public prosecutor to the police in which the person under investigation participates in a state of liberty (art. 370(1) c.p.p.)

- hearing to validate the arrest in flagrante delicto or detention (art. 391(1) c.p.p.)

- interview after the application of pre-trial personal measure (interrogatorio di garanzia, art. 294(4) c.p.p.)

- anticipated acquisition of evidence during investigation or preliminary hearing (incidente probatorio, art. 401(1) c.p.p.)

- preliminary hearing (art. 420 (1) c.p.p.)

- hearings of the abbreviated proceeding (giudizio abbreviato), through the referral made by art. 441(1) c.p.p.

- hearing for acquittal before trial (art. 469 c.p.p.)

- trial hearings in first and second instance (Tribunal, Court of Appeal, artt. 484(2) and (2 bis), 598 c.p.p.)

- hearing before the Court of Appeal following the renewal of the preliminary investigation (art. 599(3) c.p.p.)

- hearings during the enforcement proceedings (art. 666(4) c.p.p.)

- hearing before the Court of Appeal in passive extradition proceedings (art. 704(2)c.p.p.).


To these cases should also be added those in which:

- the lawyer is present but lacks the necessary requisites to exercise such an office (person not qualified to exercise the profession because s/he is not registered in the defenders' register or has been disbarred). In case of lawyers lacking a specific qualification to defend child suspects, disciplinary measures may be imposed.

- The lawyer is present but in a situation of incompatibility (e.g. s/he is defending suspects with conflicting positions).


B) On the other side, where the lawyer can participate to certain investigative acts, but such presence is not mandatory by law, an intermediate nullity (nullità intermedia) may occur (cf. again Article 178 (1) let c) c.p.p.).

This is for instance the case where a the lawyer is not notified of the time, date and place where such act will be carried out (e.g. art. 360, 364(3) c.p.p.), or where the lawyer is not allowed to immediately confer with the defendant ex Article 104 c.p.p. and the reasons for this deferral are not adquately motivated, or where the conditions of the communication with the client are not allowing adquate privacy. Illegal recording or interception of confidential information could also be punished as a criminal offence in accordance to Article 617 Italian Criminal Code.

This form of nullity is less severe than absolute nullity, although it can be deduced both by parties and ex officio.

If the defect in the act occurs before the trial, the nullity shall be deducted within the first instance trial decision; if it occurs during the trial, the nullity shall be deducted within the next instance decision (court of appeal, supreme court).

The inertia of the party or of the judge beyond such time limits produces a regularization of the invalidity.


It is important to underline that, under Italian law, no distinction is made between children and adults when it comes to the right of access to a lawyer ex Article 364 c.p.p.

Although the national legal system provides for the right to have the lawyer present during questionings performed by the Public Prosecutor, the attendance of the lawyer is not mandatory in these instances, as required by the Directive. No remedy can therefore be used to complain about the lack of defence lawyer in this context.



﻿RIGHT TO AN INDIVIDUAL ASSESSMENT

The right to an individual assessment is provided for under Italian law, but no sanctions are established in case of breaches of such obligations. However, according to some legal scholars, if in the course of the proceedings, a measure concerning the child is taken without any individual assessment, the concerned decision may be considered as affected by a nullity of general nature for the violation of the right to defence (Article 178(1)(c) c.p.p. (on whose effects, see above), cf. AA.VV., Fondamenti di procedura penale, Cedam, 2019, p. 974; V. Patanè, L'intervento dell'imputato minorenne nelle varie fasi del procedimento, in G. Giostra (ed) Il processo penale minorile, Giuffrè, 2016, p. 66.

According to others, such decision should be affected instead by the special nullity referred to in Art 125, c. 3 CCP, due to the  violation of the duty to state reasons (cf. Alberto Camon, Claudia Cesari, Marcello Daniele, Maria Lucia Di Bitonto, Daniele Negri, Paulesu Pier Paolo, Fondamenti di procedura penale (Cedam 2019), 974; Vania Patanè, ʿAccertamenti sulla personalità del minorenneʾ in Glauco Giostra (ed), Il processo penale minorile (Giuffrè 2016) 140-41; Enrico Lanza, ʿLe indagini preliminari e le misure cautelariʾ in Angelo Mangione and Antonino Pulvirenti (eds) La Giustizia Penale Minorile: Formazione, Devianza, Diritto e Processo (Giuffrè 2020) 470).


Lastly, no obligation for periodical updates of the individual assessment is provided for by Italian law; therefore, no remedy exists in case such an update is not carried out. Equally lacking is any provision allowing persons holding parental responsibility to require such an assessment.


RIGHT TO A MEDICAL EXAMINATION

Medical examination is provided for as a right under Italian law, but no sanctions are established in case of breaches of such obligations. Complaints in this regard cannot therefore be effectively raised in the Italian legal order. In case the breach amounts also to a violation of Article 3 ECHR, a claim could be raised before the Court in Strasbourg.



RIGHT TO AUDIOVISUAL RECORDING

Italian law never requires mandatory audiovisual recording of interviews, neither for adult, nor for juvenile defendants. Even in case of detained defendants, Article 141 bis only offers a non mandatory option (cf. G. Varraso, Interrogatorio in vinculis dell’imputato: tra istanze di difesa, esigenze di garanzia, ragioni di accertamento, in Riv. it. dir. proc. pen, 1999, 1429-1430). No remedy therefore exists, in case this right is not complied with.



LIMITATION TO DEPRIVATION OF LIBERTY

No specific remedy exists for violations concerning the deprivation of liberty of juvenile defendants. Also in this case, therefore, reference goes to the vast range of remedies provided for adult defendants to challenge the application of pre-trial detentive measures, and namely: the riesame (Art 309 CCP) and the appeal before the Supreme court (Art 311 CCP).



RIGHT TO A TIMELY TREATMENT

As a way to introduce an effective remedy against unreasonable length of the proceedings, in 2001a dedicated regulation had been introduced, known as Legge Pinto (Law no. 89 of 24 March 2001). This piece of legislation, available also to juvenile defendants, grants the right to a reparation for damages suffered because of the excessive length of the proceedings. To obtain such reparation, a request shall be submitted to the competent Court of Appeals. Legal scholars, however, have risen several doubts over the capacity of such procedure to really provide an effective remedy, especially with regard to defendant which may be in need of legal aid (cf., e.g., Barone F, La “Legge Pinto” nell’applicazione giurisprudenziale, in Responsabilita' Civile e Previdenza, fasc.4, 2020, 1122 ff.).



PROTECTION OF PRIVACY

Regardless of a specific prohibition to publish or in any way reveal pictures or identifying information concerning minors involved in criminal proceeding (Art 13, DPR 448/88), no specific remedy has been established in the Italian criminal procedure code to ensure potential violations are effectively remedied.

Violations of Art 13, Decree no. 448/1988 that could entail the criminal liability of the person(s) who disseminated news or pictures identifying the minor without the consent of the holders of parental responsibility, may be however punished in accordance with Article 615-bis of the Italian Criminal Code.



RIGHT TO BE ACCOMPANIED BY HOLDER OF PARENTAL RESPONSIBILITY

If the holder of the parental responsibility is not notified of the investigation and of the decree for committal to court hearings (rinvio a giudizio), the act in relation to which the notice should have been issued is affected by nullity, in accordance with Articles 178(1)(c) and 180 CCP.



RIGHT TO BE PRESENT AT TRIAL

As for adults, violations of the right to be present at trial can be raised through the specific remedy of the rescissione del giudicato, provided for by Art 629-bis CCP. The critical issues raised with regard to this tool, therefore, are applicable also in this context; above all, that the burden of proof imposed on the convicted to activate the remedy excessively restricts the effectiveness of the right to a re-trial.

When it comes to minors, however, the impact on European Arrest Warrant proceedings may be considered as less significant, in light of the already-mentioned mandatory ground for refusal provided for by Art 18, c. 1, let. i), Law no 69/2005.

items.heading: Article 20

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that staff of law enforcement authorities and of detention facilities who handle cases involving children, receive specific training to a level appropriate to their contact with children with regard to children's rights, appropriate questioning techniques, child psychology, and communication in a language adapted to the child.

provisions.textEn:
2. For the purposes of assignment to the specialised juvenile police sections, account is taken of aptitude, degrees, diplomas, qualifications in the juvenile matter and of any

specific expertise of the law enforcement candidate.


3. The administrations to which they belong, in agreement with the Ministry of Justice, take care, even jointly, of the training and refresher courses for the personnel in charge of the juvenile police sections.

5. Officials who have carried out significant activities in the juvenile sector and that anyway possess specific aptitudes and preparation are in charge of the management of centres for juvenile justice, dentention institutions and juvenile services.

6. In order to carry out technical activities, such centres can be assigned staff of social service and pedagogical expertise. Centres may also avail themselves of the collaboration of scientific and external consultants.

items.text: 2. Without prejudice to judicial independence and differences in the organisation of the judiciary across the Member States, and with due respect for the role of those responsible for the training of judges and prosecutors, Member States shall take appropriate measures to ensure that judges and prosecutors who deal with criminal proceedings involving children have specific competence in that field, effective access to specific training, or both.

provisions.textEn: The Ministry of Justice cooperates with the Consiglio Superiore della Magistratura [the independent self-governement body of the judiciary] for the realization of special training and refresher courses for magistrates and honorary judges for juvenile court officers, in the matters relating to juvenile law and juvenile problems concerning family and age development.

The chambers of the Juvenile Court of Appeal are assigned, for at least two years, magistrates selected from among the members of the courts of appeal, who have previously worked in juvenile court offices or at the offices of the giudice tutelare or that otherwise have a specific aptitude, preparation and expertise.

items.text: 3. With due respect for the independence of the legal profession and for the role of those responsible for the training of lawyers, Member States shall take appropriate measures to promote the provision of specific training as referred to in paragraph 2 to lawyers who deal with criminal proceedings involving children.
